test: none: not fixed on truck (paused under tangency-labs/solidcraft#3992); on the kernel-smlib branch (#4012), SMLib's fillet and boolean build these plates and its integration measures them within 1e-10 of the body's volume (local run, see the PR)
summary: SolidCraft's Measure on truck read the volume a 1 mm round removes along a 100 mm edge as 21.49 mm^3 on a 100 mm plate, 21.97 on a 300 mm plate and 23.47 from 500 mm (exact 21.4602; a 1 mm chamfer was exact). Its fine tessellation is meant to tighten for small radii, but the radius probe runs on a mesh sized by the part, misses the R1 arc on large plates, and leaves the chord tolerance (sag) at 1/20000 of the part: the error matches 32, 8, 4 and 4 chords on the round's quarter arc on the 100, 300, 500 and 1000 mm plates. The cases are the issue's plates (100 x D x 10, the round on the top edge at y = D), a dia. 3 through hole in the 100 and 1000 mm plates, and the plain 100 and 1000 mm plates as controls. Tolerances are 0.1 % of the feature's volume, so a volume that drifts with the part's size fails. Volumes are closed form.
